hypotheses.statement: The published G9 grammar is not executable-conformant with the current G9 V3 moving-stack specification.
hypotheses.mechanism: Current spec uses surface constructs absent from grammar.ebnf, including comparison operators and conditional blocks.
hypotheses.prediction: A parser faithful to the published operator/block subset rejects a current-spec fixture; a minimal grammar repair accepts it.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: The apparent discrepancy is only informal notation and the published grammar can parse the current spec unchanged.
hypotheses.falsifier: A production parser generated strictly from current grammar.ebnf successfully self-parses the complete unmodified G9 V3 spec with deterministic roundtrip semantics.
hypotheses.test: Local Lark baseline vs patched grammar on current G9 comparison/if fixture.

hypotheses.statement: The tested FRANK LoopDynamicsReadout/RecurrenceDecision contract can be represented using existing G9 semantic forms without adding a new ClayCode primitive.
hypotheses.mechanism: Existing record, union, Set, optional Ref, rule and capability-separation forms cover the tested loop state/readout/controller vocabulary once comparison parsing is repaired.
hypotheses.prediction: A minimally repaired executable grammar accepts the typed loop contract without adding a new semantic category.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Loop-of-loops instrumentation requires a novel primitive or bespoke loop syntax to preserve semantics safely.
hypotheses.falsifier: Production typed IR/type-effect/lowering cannot preserve at least one required loop behavior using existing forms and no typed host adapter can close the gap.
hypotheses.test: Local parser experiment on typed LoopDynamicsReadout + RecurrenceDecision fixture.

hypotheses.statement: Separating semantic_hash from contract_hash preserves set-like semantic equivalence while retaining exact provenance-bound contract identity.
hypotheses.mechanism: Only explicitly set-typed fields are deduplicated/sorted for semantic identity; exact instance structure remains in contract identity; ordered fields remain order-sensitive.
hypotheses.prediction: Duplicate/reordered set-like permits produce equal semantic hashes but distinct contract hashes; reordered ordered steps change semantic hash.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Canonicalization erases provenance-significant or order-significant differences.
hypotheses.falsifier: Property/fuzz tests find two semantically distinct typed values with the same semantic hash or semantically equal set values with unstable hashes under permitted normalization.

hypotheses.statement: A typed capability boundary can preserve expressibility without allowing textual/model output to mint execution authority.
hypotheses.mechanism: Commit eligibility depends on a valid non-revoked authority-issued capability token rather than a textual capability name.
hypotheses.prediction: Text-only, revoked and forged-issuer cases are rejected while valid authority-issued token is accepted.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: The source/runtime boundary leaks authority through symbolic capability references or unvalidated host adapters.
hypotheses.falsifier: Production FFI/effect fuzzing finds any path where model/source text alone causes an effect commit without an external valid capability/commit witness.
